prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / product-mockup. Create ONE reusable COMPUTER TERMINAL EXTERIOR TEMPLATE for ordinary civilian computers in a space station game. 1536x1024 landscape, full console front-facing orthographic 2D UI frame, no room or desk around it. User inspiration: the recognizable integrated screen-and-keyboard form of Fallout terminals, but appreciably LESS RETRO and NOT military. Do not reproduce any branded terminal.
A modern industrial civilian workstation: smooth graphite-gray powder-coated shell, softly rounded rectangular outer corners, tasteful slim aluminum monitor lip, inset dark glass, modest thickness, short sloped keyboard deck visible along bottom with compact low-profile keys, discreet ventilation on sides, one restrained cyan power light and a small amber activity light. No handles, no armored side rails, no exposed wires, no hazard stripes, no bolts everywhere, no CRT bulb, no green phosphor wash, no rust or battle damage, no wooden trim. Material should feel like durable contemporary office/scientific equipment made for a space station.
Most of image is ONE EMPTY CLEAN RECTANGULAR SCREEN in uniform near-black, suitable for overlaying different live interfaces. Do not draw ANY UI panels, icons, writing, grid, scan lines or reflection across the central empty display. Screen should occupy roughly 78% image width and 70% image height. Narrow side shoulders and generous screen usability. Bottom keyboard about 12% image height, subtle shallow key relief, small unlabelled horizontal touch strip or status recess. Top slim blank title area, no words on shell. Keep whole silhouette fully visible. Neutral graphite body with a few warm light-gray inset surfaces and cool gray bezel gives it a softer civilian identity. No giant switches or armed buttons. High-quality tactile readable 2D game interface asset with controlled fine texture; minimal perspective only keyboard slope. Opaque black display intentional; no alpha transparency needed. Deliver the FRAME ONLY, empty screen, no mockup board, no captions, no multiple variations.
